key_insight: Low-temperature annealing at 200 °C relaxes defects in mechanically alloyed FeNiTiCuAl HEA powder, making it much more cold-sprayable while keeping the metastable FCC-dominated structure largely intact.
engineering_relevance: A simple pre-anneal can markedly improve coating build-up and particle retention for difficult HEA powders, enabling denser cold-sprayed coatings without major phase changes.
method: Mechanical alloying of equiatomic FeNiTiCuAl powder followed by annealing at 200, 300, and 500 °C
XRD, Rietveld analysis, DSC, and microhardness used to track recovery vs. phase evolution
Cold spray and single-particle splat tests on the same 20–40 μm fraction under identical conditions
evidence_signal: Compared with as-milled powder, the 200 °C-treated powder showed lower microstrain/hardness and much thicker coatings, with average thickness increasing from 78 ± 5 to 204 ± 19 μm.
watch_item: Annealing above 200 °C begins to alter phase constitution and chemical homogeneity, so process windows must be tightly controlled to avoid unintended hardening or BCC/B2 formation.
paper_title: Enabling cold spray deposition of mechanically alloyed FeNiTiCuAl high-entropy alloy powder through annealing
